title: The fourth cipher riddle in a Mamluk book of ciphers, about 1325-1360 (Penn LJS 51, ff. 48r–48v and 21r)

documents.shelfmark: University of Pennsylvania, Kislak Center, LJS 51, f. 48r l.8 - 48v l.13 and f. 21r l.1-5 (OPenn images 0084_0100, 0084_0101, 0084_0046)
documents.date: correspondence of the volume about 1325-1360 (this project's dating from internal evidence); the witness is probably a 15th-century copy: Penn's record "Possibly written in Syria, in the 15th century", date "14--"

plaintext.source: The clear riddle follows its cipher on f. 21r l.7 – 21v l.2. Blind annealing on ff. 48r–48v yielded recognizable Arabic before that match.

transcription.source: OPenn master TIFFs 0084_0100, 0084_0101 and 0084_0046. The f. 21r lines come from the corpus key record 20r.8+47r.1.json, block_21r_1_5.
transcription.notes: Full text measured with --drop-first and the divider skipped (63 dividers). The original blind experiment used the f. 48r–48v portion.

system.summary: Simple substitution of invented signs for Arabic letters, right to left, with a dotted stem between words.
system.sibling_key: f. 47r key (same sign family) tried and ruled out
system.notes: The continuation adds W2 (squat alif) and EK, the horned sign used once for ح and once for ش. The original 27 labels include AY/O8 for ي and X/XN for ل.

prior_solution.where: In the same codex: the compiler broke this cipher himself, "quickly because of its ease" (21r l.6, right after the cipher's last five lines on 21r l.1-5, which a misbound quire separates from f. 48v; corpus work, targets/ljs51corpus/keys_eye/REPORT.md), and wrote the plaintext in clear on f. 21r l.7 - 21v l.2. No study of the ciphers of LJS 51 found (Penn TEI, Digital Scriptorium, DECODE, Tomokiyo, Lasry's list, web); Penn cites Transformation of Knowledge (2006), p. 43, for the manuscript (not seen). DECODE has no record of it.

conditions.human_role: None for this block beyond the corpus project's brief (transcribe and rekey every chain of LJS 51).

solution.what: OPenn master TIFFs of ff. 48r and 48v (images 0084_0100, 0084_0101) used for the transcription and crops.
Chain record 48r.8: 19 lines, 226 signs by eye, 51 groups; same sign family as the f. 47r block. Then a labelled transcription (transcription.txt v1): 229 signs, 52 groups.
Applied the f. 47r key (keys_eye/47r.1.json) to the block.

Tested by length and group pattern the verses on 49r l.6-7 (72 letters), the first five verses of the 47r riddle (about 208 letters; the 47r key does not give wa-ma at verse starts) and the compiler's eight answer-verses (about 320 letters).

anneal_sp.py: one-to-one keys, word dividers as spaces, ar-mamluk model, 6 restarts x 40,000 steps, no plaintext given. Restart 1 reached -2.51 per character and read Arabic ('... ahl aslah tathur idha b n al-layl wa-tarhal 'ind al-safah tarmiha ... wa-hiya ma'duda min na'im ahl al-janna ...'); the other five scored -2.64 to -3.24 with partial words.

Identified the annealer's text as the rhymed-prose riddle in clear on f. 21r l.7 - 21v l.2 (then catalogued under chain 20r.8). DP alignment with the key re-learned over 6 rounds (verify.py): 218 of 229 signs take their letter (95.2%); the block covers the first 232 of the riddle's 293 letters, to jammalatuhu.

Re-read every flagged position at 2-3x on the masters (recheck_2x.md): five transcription errors and six misplaced dividers corrected (229 -> 228 signs); the OM sign is qaf in both places. With transcription v2 (verify_v2.py): 220 of 228 signs (96.5%) take the key; 3 surplus signs, 7 dropped letters, all scribal slips or places where the cipher corrects the clear copy (tarmiha, yuhmad, al-qisi).
Rule-out (ruleout.txt): the decoded block (v1, 229 signs) against all 206 plaintexts of the book, share of signs in matching runs: 20r.8 0.952, next best 22r.1 0.223, median 0.092.
Prior art for the volume: no study of LJS 51 found; DECODE has no record of it.

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 228 tokens, 27 types, ar-mamluk order 4: reading -2.627 per letter; random keys -5.236 (z 5.5); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -2.841 (mean -2.911, z 5.5); annealer on the real text -2.715. Verdict: pass.

Re-read on the f. 21r master (0084_0046, crops at 2-4x, after Brice Dudout's review) the clear-copy words where the record and the cipher differ: the clear copy has tarmiha (as the cipher, record tawahhumuha), tuhmad with two dots above (same skeleton as the cipher's yuhmad, record wa-khamad), an undotted letter after al- in al-qisi/al-'asi (the cipher's qaf settles it), and jammalaha with a shadda (as the cipher, record jamaluha, so not a slip). The record misread the clear copy; the cipher corrects it only by settling the undotted qaf.

Blind-vs-blind null (null_blind.json; the docs/_validate.py annealer, 4,675 steps, every restart from a random key): best of 20 runs on the real signs -2.658; 60 shuffles of the signs, best of 2 restarts each, mean -2.992, sd 0.075, max -2.856; descriptive z 4.5; 0 of 60 shuffle maxima reached the real maximum. The unequal restart budgets preclude a permutation p-value. Replaces the n = 6 shuffled refit, which started one restart from the final key.

Independent re-run by Brice Dudout, with none of this project's code: his own 4-gram model from the same five OpenITI texts and his own annealer reached the riddle in 7 of 11 restarts (about -2.10 per sign); shuffled ciphertext, best of 12 restarts -3.18, no sense. None of 14 distinctive phrases of the riddle occurs in the five source texts; 0.7% of its 12-grams do.

Identified the 62-sign continuation on f. 21r l.1–5. The original key assigns 59 occurrences; the two additional shapes account for three more. The corpus comparison found 44 positional matches at the end of the clear prose and at most 11 at any other offset.

validation.notes: Ff. 48r–48v only. claimed per-occurrence score -2.627; polyphony 0.0; 0 unread tokens left out; annealer on the real text from random keys reached -2.715; blind-vs-blind rerun (null_blind.json): shuffled n = 60, mean -2.992, max -2.856; real blind best -2.658, descriptive z 4.5; 0 of 60 shuffle maxima reached the real maximum. The unequal restart budgets preclude a permutation p-value

outcome.method_basis: The annealer, given only the signs and an Arabic letter model, reached the text of the riddle; the clear copy on f. 21r was matched to it afterwards and the signs were aligned with that text to refine the letter assignments.
outcome.fraction_read_source: All 290 signs in transcription.txt have a recorded reading (decode.py). EK takes one of two letters according to its occurrence on f. 21r.
outcome.notes: The clear copy is the compiler’s solution of this cipher. The 220/228 alignment and the statistical validation cover ff. 48r–48v only. The continuation differs from the written copy in the closing clauses (reading.md).

reading_review.by: Claude (write-up session, a model's review, not a person's)
reading_review.note: Review of the ff. 48r–48v portion only. Read as sentences against the clear copy on f. 21r (chain 20r.8) and its translation: every rhymed-prose clause builds; the seven slips are emended in [ ] from the clear copy, and three places follow the cipher against the record of the clear copy. Re-checked 27 Nov 2026 against the f. 21r image after Brice Dudout's review: the record misread ترميها, تحمد and جمّلها; the jammalaha emendation dropped. No Arabist has checked the reading yet.

texts.summary: A riddle in rhymed prose (the fourth enciphered piece of the series), which the compiler writes in clear on f. 21r: something soft of sides and wide of flanks that visits at night and leaves at dawn, counted among the bliss of Paradise and spread out 'by a permitted contract'. The compiler gives the answer as the raised couches (furush marfūʿa) of Sūrat al-Wāqiʿa. It closes by telling the reader to give thanks on settling there.
